title: Myelin, nodes, and speed
objective: Explain how myelination and axon diameter set conduction velocity.

steps.title: Jumping down the axon
steps.body: **[[myelin|Myelin]]** is an insulating wrap broken by gaps, the **[[node of Ranvier|nodes of Ranvier]]**. The [[action potential]] regenerates only at the nodes and 'jumps' between them — **[[saltatory conduction]]** — which is far faster than creeping along a bare membrane.

visual.alt: Two axons of the same size fire from the same start. On the myelinated axon the spike regenerates only at the nodes of Ranvier and jumps from node to node to the far end (✓ arrives first). On the unmyelinated axon it creeps along the bare membrane and is still less than halfway along when the animation holds.
visual.caption: Jumping node to node is far faster than creeping along bare membrane.

steps.prompt: Why does myelination speed up conduction?
options: The signal regenerates only at nodes and jumps between them
Myelin studs the whole axon with extra sodium channels
Myelin makes the axon much thinner along its full length
It lets the axon skip its refractory period after a spike
steps.explanation: Saltatory conduction means the spike leaps node to node instead of propagating continuously, saving time at every stretch of membrane.

variants.setup: A myelinated and an unmyelinated axon of equal diameter fire.
variants.reveal: Saltatory conduction lets the myelinated axon jump node to node, conducting faster.

steps.prompt: Besides myelin, what else raises **[[conduction velocity]]**?
options: Fewer sodium channels at the nodes
steps.explanation: Thicker axons conduct faster (less internal resistance). That's why large myelinated Aα and Aβ fibers are the fastest and thin unmyelinated C fibers the slowest.

variants.setup: Two myelinated axons differ only in diameter.
variants.reveal: Larger diameter lowers internal resistance, so the thicker axon is faster.

steps.setup: A disease strips myelin from a sensory nerve (demyelination).
options: Slowed or blocked conduction and garbled sensation
Faster and noticeably cleaner conduction than before
No change at all, since the axons are still intact
steps.reveal: Without myelin the spike must crawl continuously or fails between the (now naked) stretches, so conduction slows or blocks — the basis of demyelinating sensory symptoms.

variants.prompt: Demyelination of a sensory nerve tends to cause…
options: No change, since the axons stay intact
variants.explanation: Losing myelin removes saltatory conduction, slowing or blocking the signal.
